novel_mechanics_found: bp35 is a vertical-tower gravity puzzle with a camera that follows the player (all ACTION6 clicks are display/camera-relative). Five mechanics discovered this session, none recorded in the registry before: (1) GRAVITY SWITCHES - color-8 framed blocks, often buried inside solid wall; clicking one flips GLOBAL gravity (up<->down) and CONSUMES the switch (one-shot; its cell becomes air, which can also unblock a corridor). Levels are budgeted with a limited number of flips. (2) GOAL DIAMONDS - a small color-7 plus/diamond sprite; touching it (even mid-fall while gravity carries you through its tile) completes the level. L4's win was flipping gravity so the player 'falls up' through a floating diamond. (3) TOGGLE BLOCKS - color-12 framed 5x5 blocks toggle solid <-> open (open state renders as a 3x3 X of color 12) on every click, at ANY distance; open-X cells are safely passable and the solid state is a walkable ceiling/shelf. The three X's guarding a ceiling gap can be toggled solid to walk beneath pillar traps. (4) PILLARS - color-15 columns with a B0B (11-0-11) eye pair at one end; the eye end faces away from the anchor wall and KILLS on contact (rising into a hanging pillar's eyes, or falling onto a standing pillar's eyes). They guard most vertical channels; the safe channel is always the one without a pillar over/under it. (5) E-TILE DOORS (color-14) - one-shot doors embedded in bands; opening one reveals a hidden shaft of UNKNOWN depth below/above it. Some shafts are real passages (4+ tiles), at least one is a 1-tile sealed pocket that soft-locks the level (attempt-2 pocket under L5 pair#1 left door). Door-open clicks appear proximity/state-gated in a way not fully modeled: the same coordinates opened a door in one run and failed in an identical-looking state in another (see gotchas).
narrative: Replayed the 57-action banked prefix to verified level 2, then solved LEVEL 3 (toggle-block staircase + E-slot ascent through a scrolling vertical tower, ending by walking into a color-7 diamond) and LEVEL 4 (a three-gravity-switch routing puzzle: ride the first flip down to the door band, drop through a door into a side pocket, flip up to hug the underside of an E platform, flip down to land on a 2x2 E cluster, open it downward past a pillar gap, then use a fourth buried switch to fall UP into the floating diamond). Ran the offline reproduction gate myself on the full 121-action line from a fresh reset: reached_level=4, reproduced=True. Spent the remaining budget on LEVEL 5 recon: it is a wider multi-screen tower with chained E-door descents. Found and mapped the main descent tree; every branch currently ends in a soft-lock (1-tile door pocket, or a spike-guarded trap pocket where both floor doors sit directly above upward-facing pillar eyes), and the second gravity switch needed to return upward was never located. Stopped at 298 of 500 env steps with the L3+L4 bank verified rather than risk an unverifiable half-attempt on L5.
gotchas: Row 63 of every frame is a HUD action counter (fills one cell of color 15 per action, resets each level), not world content.
The env mutates frame buffers in place - deep-copy any grid you want to compare later; diffing two live frame objects gives garbage.

All ACTION6 clicks are camera-relative display coordinates. The camera re-centers after ANY vertical player movement (even 1-tile drops), so never reuse click coordinates computed before a fall/rise - re-read the frame first. My first L3 attempt died to a 6px-stale coordinate.

Gravity switches (color 8) are ONE-SHOT and clickable only while on-screen. Flipping gravity at the wrong column is instant death (you rise/fall into a pillar's B0B eyes). L4 has exactly 4 switches and needs all 4 in order: top switch (fall to door band), pocket switch (rise to platform underside), pocket-visible switch (fall to E cluster), bottom buried switch (rise into the diamond).
Pillar kill rule: the B0B eye end faces away from its anchor wall; contact with the eye end kills, the anchor end and sides are inert (walking on top of a band whose pillars hang below is safe).

Toggle-block X state is passable and harmless to walk through horizontally; identical-looking X glyphs in L3's first gap are also just open toggle blocks, but rising through one that has a pillar above it is death - solidify them (1 click each) to create a safe walking ceiling.

E doors hide shafts of unknown depth. L5 pair#1: right door = real 4-tile shaft, left door = 1-tile sealed pocket = unrecoverable soft-lock (no step-up/jump exists; env.reset() restarts the CURRENT level, which is the only escape).

Door-open semantics are not fully modeled: clicking a door you stand on worked in L4 and in one L5 run, but an identical-looking click failed in another L5 run (door stayed closed, action consumed). Until resolved, prefer opening doors while standing BESIDE them, and re-verify the door actually opened before walking onto it.

L5 (unsolved) map notes: start hugging under the band, 4R then click the switch at (51,39) to fall down the col-6/7 channel; first landing pair sits in a recess (cannot walk off left); descent chain right-door -> pair-B -> pair-C -> row-56 band -> funnel at cols 19-29 -> trap pair with upward pillar eyes directly beneath BOTH doors (opening either = death; the pocket is otherwise sealed). The diamond is in a top-left chamber behind a 3x2 E block whose top is guarded by 3 hanging pillars; the intended return path upward (second switch) was NOT found - candidate unexplored leads: the sealed X-room chamber (rows 33-43 x cols 18-30 relative to pair-B view), the col-2 shaft bottom, and whether pocket floors are hidden E caps openable from inside.
